claims.text: The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Equiatomic CoCrFeNi and HfNbTaTiZr are representative target alloy systems.
The method is intended for both solid and high-melting liquid states of the alloys.
The fixed-form EAM reference should be replaced by an active-learning machine-learned potential.
The proposed MLP will be iteratively trained on diverse ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations from the liquid state.
The MLP will use many-body local-environment descriptors such as SOAP.
The applicable systems are typically four- or five-component, near-equiatomic alloys.
The intervention applies at or near the alloys' high melting temperatures.
High-temperature HEA liquids exhibit rich configurational diversity.
Many-body local-environment descriptors allow the MLP to capture a wide range of atomic configurations and chemical environments.
Active learning identifies regions of high uncertainty in the liquid configuration space.
Iterative refinement in uncertain regions ensures high fidelity between MLP predictions and ab initio energies.
Improved representation of liquid configurations increases reference-target phase-space overlap during thermodynamic integration.
Increased phase-space overlap reduces mismatch in thermodynamic-integration free-energy paths relative to EAM references.
The MLP will reduce TI path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Free-energy differences computed using the MLP reference will approach a fully converged ab initio MD benchmark within a specified error margin.
Traditional EAM references as implemented in TOR-TILD provide the comparison baseline.
Applicability to substantially off-stoichiometric alloys and lower temperatures is undetermined.
The anticipated 50% reduction is based on evidence from elemental and binary liquid simulations.
The hypothesis is falsified if mismatch reduction is below approximately 20% or the free-energy discrepancy exceeds 5% relative to the ab initio benchmark.
